selected_texts.text: Anthropic says it must forecast compute needs and make commitments months or years before day-to-day use, often with limited ability to adjust them.
Anthropic warns that if actual requirements differ materially from its projections, it may have insufficient compute or excess compute that remains underutilized.

As of June 30, 2026, the company reported about $265.6 billion of future fixed or minimum purchase obligations under compute and infrastructure agreements with terms from one to 20 years. Other agreements without fixed or minimum dollar commitments are not included in that amount.
As of June 30, 2026, estimated future undiscounted obligations for leases not yet commenced were $321.4 billion; some arrangements were subject to contractual conditions.
The author writes: "1/16 the ai industry is making an unusual bet: buy compute for years, sell intelligence by the token."
The author writes: "the three with spacex, nscale and lambda are maximums anthropic can walk away from or pays only on delivery."

The AI Insider presents a bullish case that rapid revenue growth and improvements in compute spending relative to revenue could support better economics if the relationship continues; it explicitly treats persistence as a conditional proposition.

The AI Insider presents a bearish case that long-duration compute obligations, uncertain growth, and reliance on partners that are also competitors could matter for the company and its future valuation.

control_result.conclusion: Anthropic faces financial and operational exposure to compute forecasting errors, as its long-term, multi-year fixed or minimum infrastructure commitments and uncommenced lease obligations cannot be easily adjusted if actual demand deviates from expectations.
